title: The Groan Cup
pitch: A velvet-curtain comedy club where the visitor referees a knockout cup of invented one-liners, picking the funnier of two over and over. Behind the curtain the page fits a Bradley-Terry ranking after every vote, chooses the next pairing that teaches it the most, and then pits the visitor's leaderboard against a panel of silly rule-based judge bots (the pun counter, the length snob, the vowel enthusiast). The payoff is a shareable verdict card: how stable your taste is, which jokes were glazed in the kiln, and which judge bot thinks most like you.
whyNow: A 2026 preprint on tournament-style humor ranking (pairwise judgments aggregated with Bradley-Terry, with adaptive Swiss pairing) is the fresh hook; the mechanic itself is timeless. Humor is owed this week.

research.summary: A 2026 arXiv preprint (HumorRank) ranks humor generation by running theory-informed pairwise preference judgments in a tournament and aggregating them with Bradley-Terry estimation, using adaptive Swiss pairing and checking rank stability with Kendall tau between independent judges. The page rebuilds only that ranking intuition with human votes on a small bundled set of original, invented one-liners; it reproduces none of the paper's results and shows no model scores. Bradley-Terry itself is standard, well-documented background (strength scores from pairwise wins, closely related to Elo, needs a connected comparison graph), so the in-browser fit (an iterative maximum-likelihood update) is honest and small. Paper-specific details come from one paper seen through arXiv and a mirror and stay marked unverified.

facts.claim: The Bradley-Terry model assigns each item a latent strength and predicts pairwise outcomes from the strength gap; equal strengths give a 50 percent chance each (as seen in search results on 2026-10-12).

As of 2026-10-12, per the arXiv listing 2604.19786 (HumorRank), humor generation is ranked from pairwise judgments aggregated with Bradley-Terry; this was seen only via arXiv and a mirror, so it is reported, not confirmed.
The alphaxiv mirror shows version 2 of the HumorRank paper submitted on 1 June 2026 and labelled as submitted to COLM 2026 (reported, unconfirmed).
Bradley-Terry fitting needs a connected comparison graph, so disconnected groups of items cannot be ranked jointly (vendor documentation, one source).

inspirations: pairwise voting arenas for model leaderboards

design.coreLoop: Two invented one-liners appear on a velvet stage; the visitor picks the funnier. Each vote refits Bradley-Terry strengths and the next pairing is chosen where the ranking is least certain (adaptive Swiss-style), so the leaderboard visibly sharpens and sometimes flips. After a round of about 20 votes the visitor sees their ranking, a bootstrap confidence band per joke, a stability score (Kendall tau between the first and second half of their own votes) and agreement with each silly judge bot. The second minute rewards trying to break the bots; the tenth rewards chasing a stable, repeatable taste or sharing a deck of votes by URL.
sophisticationHooks: Live Bradley-Terry fit by iterative maximum likelihood, with bootstrap confidence bands drawn per joke
Adaptive pairing that picks the most informative matchup while keeping the comparison graph connected
Five or six deterministic judge bots (pun counter, length snob, vowel enthusiast, alliteration fan) ranked against the visitor with Kendall tau
Vote history encoded in the URL hash so a verdict card can be shared and replayed
design.scopeForOneDay: Build: 24 to 30 original, clean, invented one-liners written by the team (no real people, brands or quotes), stage UI with velvet curtain and kiln-glaze result styling in CSS and SVG, BT solver, adaptive pairing, bootstrap bands, judge bots, hash state, about panel citing the preprint. Cut: any language model, any claim about model rankings, live fetching, accounts, audio.
risks: The paper details (Bradley-Terry, adaptive Swiss pairing, COLM 2026 note) were seen via arXiv text and one mirror only; the page presents them as 'as of 2026-10-12, per arXiv 2604.19786' and reproduces no result from the paper.
Jokes must be original and inoffensive; a review pass strips anything targeting a person or group, and no jokes are copied from anywhere.
Humor is subjective, so the page frames bots as silly heuristics and never as measuring funniness or standing in for the paper's model judges.
The paper is from spring 2026, not this week; the hook is 'recent preprint' rather than breaking news.
